title: Photon pair antibunching and second-order correlations between pair events
authors: Chien-Chang Chen, Ite A. Yu, Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract: We introduce the pair second-order correlation function $g_{\textrm{pairs}}^{\left(2\right)}=\left\langle \left(P^{\dagger}\right)^{2}P^{2}\right\rangle /\left\langle P^{\dagger}P\right\rangle ^{2}$, defined through the pair operator $P^{\dagger}=a^{\dagger}b^{\dagger}$, to characterize second-order correlations and pair bunching and antibunching in photon-pair creation processes. This quantity directly probes correlations between pair-generation events within a single two-mode quantum state, providing access to the intrinsic pair-generation process beyond conventional single-mode or heralded second-order correlations, which do not directly capture correlations between pair events. Values of $g_{\textrm{pairs}}^{\left(2\right)}$ greater than, equal to, or less than unity correspond respectively to pair bunching, Poissonian pair statistics, and pair antibunching. Using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, we further show that all classical two-mode fields described by a positive Glauber--Sudarshan \ensuremath{P}-function satisfy $g_{\textrm{pairs}}^{\left(2\right)}\geq1$, so that pair antibunching is classically forbidden and constitutes an unambiguous signature of nonclassicality. We evaluate $g_{\textrm{pairs}}^{\left(2\right)}$ for several representative quantum states and show, in particular, that even arbitrarily weak two-mode squeezed vacuum states exhibit pair bunching. Comparison with heralded second-order correlations highlights the complementary information provided by these observables. The proposed correlation function is experimentally accessible via standard coincidence measurements, requires no phase reference or state reconstruction, and remains invariant under uniform loss.
summary: The paper introduces the pair second-order correlation function, $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$, to characterize statistics of photon pairs generated from two-mode quantum states. It establishes that observing antibunching ($g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}} < 1$) is a signature of nonclassicality because it violates a bound applicable to all classical fields. This observable is experimentally accessible via standard coincidence measurements.
main_problem: To establish a rigorous, experimentally accessible, and loss-tolerant benchmark for genuinely quantum pair emission statistics by characterizing correlations between pair events.
main_result: The pair second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$ provides an unambiguous signature of nonclassicality because observing $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}} < 1$ violates the classical bound derived from positive P-functions.
method: Theoretical derivation using the pair operator $P^\dagger = a^\dagger b^\dagger$, combined with applying the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to establish classical bounds for two-mode fields.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on two-mode quantum states, particularly the Two-Mode Squeezed Vacuum (TMSV) state, and its behavior under various approximations like finite-order truncations.
key_observables: Pair second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$, which quantifies pair bunching ($>1$), Poissonian statistics ($=1$), or antibunching ($<1$).
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($\lambda$) and mean photon number ($ ar{n}$); the comparison is drawn between $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$ and heralded single-mode correlations.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results derived from exact quantum calculations against bounds established using classical field representations (positive Glauber–Sudarshan P-function).
figures_summary: Figures compare the pair correlation function $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$ to heralded correlations for TMSV states, showing how bunching/antibunching changes with mean photon number and truncation order.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the novel observable $g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}}$, derives its physical meaning (bunching vs. antibunching), establishes the classical bound ($g^{(2)}_{	ext{pairs}} \ge 1$), and then evaluates this function for representative quantum states like TMSV.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-standard diagnostic tool in quantum optics that directly probes correlations between pair generation events, offering a distinct advantage over conventional single-mode or heralded correlation measurements.
